To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a well-defined variational principle in odd-dimensional Ad S gravity can be obtained by imposing boundary conditions on the extrinsic curvature and the Lorentz curvature; 2) the boundary term that is needed to obtain a well-defined variatio nal principle also regularizes the Euclidian action, and gives the correct thermodynamic behavior of black hole solutions; 3) the conserved charges are computed directly from the asymptotic Killing vector fields, without the need to refer to any background

(a) A background independent, Lorentz covariant, alternative method to the counterterms method is presented for the computation of conserved charges in AdS gravity in odd-dimensional spacetime; (b) The method reproduces the correct black hole entropy in all odd dimensions; (c) The method is used to compute the vacuum energy for odd-dimensional topological AdS solutions, which matches the conjectured value of \cite{Emparen-Johnson-MSyers}.
we have developed a background-independent, Lorenotz-covariant method to compute conserved quantities in odd-dimensional gravity.

the vacuum energy is given by the sum of the boundary terms in the gravitational action.

the vacuum energy in odd-dimensional gravity can be consistently defined in terms of a boundary term which is a generalization of the Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary term.

, in odd dimensions, the vacuum energy of odd-dimensional AdS spacetime is non-zero and depends on the dimension.
